description: Renovate owns every dependency in this repo (it replaced Dependabot, whose bun-ecosystem support silently skipped aliased packages and unified versions across workspace manifests). Global posture: `rangeStrategy: bump` so in-range releases still arrive as visible PRs, and `minimumReleaseAge: 7 days` to mirror the bunfig.toml supply-chain soak gate, so Renovate never proposes a version `bun install` would refuse.

packageRules.description: `typescript` is deliberately held on 6.x: it supplies the compiler API that TypeScript 7.0 dropped, and @vercel/node resolves `typescript` from the project to compile api/**/*.ts at deploy time — a 7.x here silently breaks the serverless build. Minors/patches on 6.x are fine. Lift this once TypeScript 7.1 restores the programmatic API. Match on depName so this does not also catch the typescript-7 alias below.

The TypeScript 7 compiler is installed as an npm alias (typescript-7 = npm:typescript@^7.0.2). Match on depName, NOT packageName: the alias resolves to packageName `typescript`, which would also match the 6.x compiler-API pin above. The global `rangeStrategy: bump` is load-bearing here — under `replace`, an in-range release like 7.1.0 (the one we are waiting for) would satisfy ^7.0.2 and produce no PR.

react and react-dom must be the EXACT same version — react-dom refuses to boot otherwise (react.dev/warnings/version-mismatch). Dependabot repeatedly bumped one without the other (issue #208 / PR #201: react-dom 19.2.8 against react 19.2.7) and such a PR always fails CI. Group them and their @types into a single PR across every manifest so they can never desync. config:recommended's group:monorepos would group react/react-dom anyway; this rule makes the invariant explicit and adds the types packages.

Tailwind is at two different majors on purpose: v4 for the web app, v3 for apps/mobile (NativeWind v4 hard-requires v3). Renovate reads each manifest separately, so it can hold the two apart — Dependabot could not, which is how its PR #187 rewrote apps/mobile from ^3.4.17 to ^4.3.3 while calling itself a patch bump.

Hard ceiling: apps/mobile must never be offered Tailwind v4. NativeWind v4 refuses to run against it ('NativeWind only supports Tailwind CSS v3'), and nothing in CI would catch the break because the mobile build script is a no-op.

Expo SDK-managed native modules: `expo install` owns these versions. Each Expo SDK release pins an exact compatible set (node_modules/expo/bundledNativeModules.json), and `npx expo install --fix` is the only correct way to change them — bot PRs propose versions the SDK does not support, and nothing catches it because no CI job builds the native app (the failure only appears at `eas build` or on a device). Upgrade deliberately: `cd apps/mobile && npx expo install expo@^<next> --fix`, then `npx expo-doctor` and a device build. `expo-*`/`@expo/*` wildcards also catch third-party `expo-quick-actions`, whose compatibility tracks the SDK anyway. NOT listed on purpose: `react`/`react-dom` (shared with the web app; apps/mobile deviates from Expo's pin via `expo.install.exclude`), and react-native-vision-camera / react-native-mmkv / react-native-nitro-modules / react-native-reorderable-list / nativewind (native, but not in Expo's bundled list, so bumps are legitimate — they still deserve a device build before merging).
